blogs.title: The Intrinsic Requirement: When Prior Possession Is Evidence of Ownership
blogs.description: In *United States v. Cutbank*, the Eighth Circuit rejected the defense's Rule 404(b) motion to suppress testimony regarding prior encounters with the gun. This post analyzes the 'intrinsic evidence' exception, explaining how the 8th Circuit established that prior possession of a specific firearm is not merely character evidence but essential proof of ownership and control necessary to establish guilt for the current possession charge.

blogs.title: Beyond the ACCA Cap: Why Specific Firearms Enhancements Survive the Guideline Calculation
blogs.description: Cutbank argued that applying the four-level firearm possession enhancement under USSG § 2K2.1(b)(6)(B) following an Armed Career Criminal Act (ACCA) conviction violated § 3553(a). This post dissects the court's reasoning that the ACCA sets the baseline offense level, but does not immunize the sentence from specific, egregious enhancement provisions that add necessary granular detail to the sentencing structure.

blogs.title: When the Court Says 'Irrelevant': Hearsay, Limiting Instructions, and the No-Instruction Precedent
blogs.description: A strategic procedural issue in federal trials is the necessity of limiting instructions for out-of-court statements. In this case, the district court affirmed the dismissal of defecting hearsay instructions after the declarant testified live. This post explores how the 8th Circuit applied the Confrontation Clause in *Battle* and *Charboneau* to determine when limiting instructions are truly required versus when a witness's presence satisfies the constitutional requirement.
